supplement.where: Included Appendices A-D: A, User Study Results (p. 20, Figures 13-14); B.1-B.5, Prompts (pp. 20-24); C, Self-designed Scales for User Study (p. 24); D, More Creative Blends: Additional Cases (pp. 24-25, Figure 15). Supplementary material is also mentioned in Section 4.3.3 (p. 8) and Section 6.4 (p. 13); no separate URL is given.
supplement.holds: User-study output examples, prompt scripts, self-designed questionnaire items, and additional system examples. No additional inferential-statistics tables are included. The output examples do not establish that the full underlying dataset is provided.

paper_design_summary: Creative Blends uses GPT-3.5-turbo, ConceptNet, and DALL-E 3 to support metaphorical visual-blend ideation; development was informed by interviews and think-aloud design work with eight practitioners (p. 4, Sections 3-3.1; pp. 7-8, Sections 4.3.1-4.3.3). In a separate counterbalanced within-subject evaluation, 24 university students and faculty used Creative Blends and a ChatGPT (GPT-3.5 with DALL-E 3) plus Google Search baseline for an 8-minute task each, with no stated random assignment of order (pp. 9-10, Sections 6-6.2). Reported quantitative outcomes are participants' questionnaire ratings of usability, cognitive load, satisfaction, creativity support and metaphoricity; no independent output creativity or across-person diversity score is reported (pp. 10-13, Section 6.3).

studies.label: Within-subject user study: Creative Blends vs ChatGPT plus Google Search baseline

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the two systems and the two design topics (T1, T2) within person, through a Latin square of four sequences: (a) T1 (Baseline) - T2 (Creative Blends), (b) T2 (Baseline) - T1 (Creative Blends), (c) T1 (Creative Blends) - T2 (Baseline), and (d) T2 (Creative Blends) - T1 (Baseline). The paper says counterbalanced and does not say the sequences were assigned at random.
assignment.quote: To maintain experimental balance, we employed a Latin Square design, yielding four possible sequences:
assignment.locator: p. 10, Section 6.2; also p. 9, Figure 6 caption and Section 6

arms.name: Creative Blends
arms.description: The authors' system: GPT-3.5-turbo with ConceptNet proposes metaphor-related objects and attributes, and DALL-E 3 generates the blended images

arms.name: Baseline
arms.description: ChatGPT (GPT-3.5 with DALL-E 3) and Google Search side by side in one interface

participants.who: Local university students and faculty members aged 20 to 31 (12 female, 12 male), half from computer science and half from design, with interest in visual design and experience with conversational AI and text-to-image models; each person used both systems
participants.quote: We enlisted a total of 24 participants (12 female, 12 male) aged 20 to 31 (Mean = 24.08, SD = 3.31) through online advertising and word-of-mouth. The participants were local university students and faculty members
participants.locator: p. 10, Sections 6.1-6.2 (participant count and within-subject procedure); pp. 12-13, Sections 6.3.3-6.3.5 (paired t(23) tests). Table 1 on p. 11 gives t statistics without degrees of freedom.

ai_tool.name_model: Creative Blends (GPT-3.5-turbo, ConceptNet, DALL-E 3); baseline ChatGPT (GPT-3.5 with DALL-E 3) plus Google Search
ai_tool.how_used: Participants typed prompts and selected objects and attributes; both conditions generated images with DALL-E 3. The contrast is between two AI configurations.

task.description: Produce visual-blend ideas for two abstract expressions: 'Smoking is like a warm welcome to death' (T1) and 'Knowledge guides the hope of our life' (T2), one per system
task.duration: 8 minutes per task after a 4-minute tutorial; whole session at most 60 minutes

outcomes.name: Metaphoricity (participants' 7-point rating of the metaphorical relationship in the generated outputs)
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: Creative Blends mean 5.655 (SD 0.974) vs Baseline 5.047 (SD 1.193); t = 2.276, p = 0.032 (Table 1); text: t(23) = -2.276, p = 0.032, Cohen's d = 0.558

outcomes.name: Outcome satisfaction: diversity (participants' satisfaction with the diversity of the system output)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Participant satisfaction with the diversity of their own system outputs; this is not a scored diversity measure across different people's outputs (p. 12, Section 6.3.3; p. 24, Appendix C.1, Q2).

contrasts.reported: Creative Blends mean 5.380 (SD 1.345) vs Baseline 3.670 (SD 1.274); t = 5.058, p < 0.001 (Table 1); text: t(23) = -5.058, d = 1.305. Overall satisfaction 5.080 (SD 1.283) vs 3.960 (SD 1.367), t = 2.609, p = 0.016

outcomes.name: Creativity Support Index, exploration item (participants' rating of how well the system supported exploration)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: The modified CSI exploration item rates the system's support for the participant's exploration process, rather than assigning a creativity score to the generated output (p. 12, Section 6.3.4).

contrasts.reported: Creative Blends mean 5.708 (SD 1.160) vs Baseline 4.083 (SD 1.886); t = 2.985, p = 0.007 (Table 1); text: t(23) = -2.985, d = 1.038. Expressiveness 5.167 (SD 1.167) vs 4.375 (SD 1.689), t = 1.807, p = 0.084

studies.label: Formative interviews and think-aloud visual-blend design study

assignment.what_was_assigned: No AI treatment or comparison condition is reported. Practitioners discussed prior design experience and completed a visual-blend design task while thinking aloud; the study elicited design challenges and requirements for AI support. A condition-comparison structure is not applicable.
assignment.quote: We emphasized the design process over the final product, requesting participants to detail the evolution of their ideas.

participants.who: Eight design practitioners: three full-time design professionals and five design students; four worked in advertising and four in graphic design. All had formal visual-design education and experience incorporating visual metaphors into their work.
participants.quote: Three participants were full-time design professionals, while the remaining five were design students who integrated visual metaphors into their personal projects.

ai_tool.how_used: No AI intervention is described. Participants reflected on desired AI tools and support for visual-blend design (p. 4, Section 3.1).

task.description: Create visual blends for 'Exercise fuels your body like vitamins' while thinking aloud; discuss previous design experience, challenges and desired AI support. The focus was the design process, with no scored creativity or diversity outcome (p. 4, Section 3.1; pp. 4-5, Section 3.2).

eligibility.reason: The evaluation analyzed 24 people, each using both AI systems (p. 10, Sections 6.1-6.2; paired t(23) tests in pp. 12-13, Sections 6.3.3-6.3.5), below the 50-person threshold. System/task order was counterbalanced with a Latin square, but random assignment of order is not stated (p. 9, Figure 6; p. 10, Section 6.2), so criterion 1 remains unclear. All reported quantitative outcomes are self-reported usability, cognitive load, satisfaction, process support or perceived metaphoricity, with no qualifying creativity or across-person diversity score (pp. 10-13, Section 6.3; p. 24, Appendix C). The eight-practitioner formative interview/think-aloud study has no randomized AI comparison or scored creativity/diversity outcome (pp. 4-5, Sections 3-3.2), and its participants are not added to the evaluation count. Neither study supplies core or eligible context evidence.

one_line_finding: In a within-subject study of 24 people, participants rated outputs from Creative Blends as more metaphorical than outputs from a ChatGPT plus Google Search baseline (5.655 vs 5.047 on a 7-point scale, p = 0.032) and were more satisfied with output diversity (5.380 vs 3.670, p < 0.001), all self-reported (p. 11, Table 1).
notes: Appendix C.2, Q5 (p. 24) specifies a participant rating of the generated outcome's aesthetic quality on a 7-point Likert scale from 'Extremely unattractive' to 'Extremely attractive'. No numerical result for this item is reported in Table 1 (p. 11) or the results text (pp. 10-13, Section 6.3); its unreported contrast statistics are null, and it supplies no additional confirmed creativity effect. The retained questionnaire outcomes are descriptive self-report context. The formative study (S2) and evaluation (S1) remain separate study records; participant overlap is not stated and their counts are not added.
